title: 2026-11-30 JIT SSO SCIM Role Curation Workshop with Strandline Health
summary: Kickoff workshop to map Strandline's Just-In-Time (JIT) SSO and SCIM flow into Redwood's RBAC model. Primary concerns: least-privilege role granularity, SCIM provisioning cadence, audit log retention, KMS key management, data residency for EU patients. Agreed to run a short pilot and exchange security artefacts.
topics: JIT SSO flow and IdP assertions
SCIM provisioning cadence and attribute mappings
Audit log storage and retention policy
next_steps: Redwood to share SOC 2 Type II report, ISO summary deck, and pen-test addendum.
Customer to provide example IdP metadata and current SCIM attribute list.
Schedule pilot kickoff (2-week pilot) and confirm EU region for data residency.
SE to run a simulated SCIM push in staging with example users and report mapping conflicts.
action_items: Lydia Park | Share SOC2, ISO docs, and pen-test summary | 2026-12-03
Evan Chu | Prepare staging SCIM push script and role-mapping template | 2026-12-07
Maya Rios | Provide IdP SAML metadata, SCIM attributes, and current RBAC CSV | 2026-12-02
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-11-30 | Start: 15:00 PST | Duration: ~72 minutes
Attendees: Lydia Park (Redwood AE), Evan Chu (Redwood SE), Maya Rios (Strandline Security Lead), Tom Keller (Platform Eng), Priya Malhotra (Head IT)

Summary (auto): quick workshop to align on JIT SSO, SCIM provisioning, and role curation; main ask is least-privilege templates and audit/log retention clarity.

00:00 Lydia (Redwood AE): hey everyone, thanks for coming, we'll give a quick 5 minute overview then jump into your IdP and SCIM questions. um Evan and I will lead the RBAC mapping portion.
00:18 Maya (Strandline): thanks Lydia, appreciate it. high level we want JIT SSO for self-serve onboarding but also strict role gates so new users dont get too many privileges.
00:26 Tom (Customer): and we care about SCIM sync frequency, we have a nightly sync today, is that ok? we want near real-time for contractors.
00:35 Evan (Redwood SE): yeah, good question. Redwood supports SCIM push and incremental deltas; typical cadence is near real-time for user events, but we also have a nightly bulk reconcile. for JIT we rely on SAML assertions to create the user and then SCIM to reconcile attributes within the first hour, so the pattern works.
01:02 Priya (Customer): can you explain how JIT interacts with our IdP claims? like what attributes you need to onboard and then map to roles?
01:12 Evan: sure. we usually require: email, name, group claims, and an optional 'entitlement' claim if you have one. group claims map to role templates. note, sometimes group names differ across IdPs so we recommend a short canonicalization step in SCIM mapping.
01:35 Maya: that canonicalization step — is it something you do server-side or we configure on our IdP? we prefer minimal IdP changes.
01:42 Evan: we can do server-side mapping rules in Redwood Console rules engine. it's a lightweight transform, like strip prefix, map alias to canonical role. example: 'dev-ops' and 'devops' both map to the 'developer' role.
01:54 Lydia: just to add, for least-privilege we push small role templates — e.g. 'read-only support', 'developer limited', 'admin escalated' — and advocate for separation of duties. you can combine templates per user based on group memberships.
02:10 Tom: ok, how do you handle time-limited elevation? e.g. contractor needs elevated access for two days.
02:16 Evan: we have ephemeral roles via session tokens and can integrate with your ticketing system for approvals. Redwood issues time-bound temporary grants and logs them to the audit trail. there's an API to query active grants.
02:28 Maya: speaking of logs — what's your retention and how fine-grained are the audit events? we need to show access to PHI for audits.
02:34 Lydia: audits capture token-level usage, role grants, SCIM events, SAML assertions, and model selection (for inference calls). retention depends on your plan — we can keep 1 year standard, options for longer retention for enterprise. exportable to your SIEM via syslog or S3.
02:53 Priya: is the log content PII/PHI redacted? we cannot store patient identifiers in third party logs.
02:59 Evan: we redact request payloads by default; metadata like user_id (internal) and role changes remain. for PHI-sensitive fields we recommend field-level masking before they reach Redwood or use VPC/private deployment variant where logs stay in your network and your KMS governs encryption.
03:20 Maya: hmm ok. and KMS — can we use our own CMK? key rotation policy?
03:26 Lydia: yes, Private deployments support customer-managed keys (CMKs) via KMS/HSM integrations. For Hosted, we support envelope encryption with customer keys in some regions. rotation policies are supported; we can provide the KMS connector playbook.
03:39 Tom: data residency — our EU patients must have inference results, logs, and tokens stay in EU region. does Redwood let us pin region?
03:46 Lydia: absolutely. Redwood Private (VPC) or region-pinned hosted endpoints can be configured to store data in the EU region only. there are nuances around backups and metadata that we'll outline in the compliance doc.
03:58 Evan: quick note — when pinning to EU, some third-party integrations might still cross regions unless you deploy connectors in-region. we'll map that out.
04:10 Maya: good. now about SCIM attribute mapping — we'll share our current attribute list but we have a couple of custom attributes: 'site_location' and 'patient_data_access_level'. how do those fit into role mapping?
04:24 Evan: custom attributes map to role rules. e.g. 'patient_data_access_level: pii_read' can be used to allow a 'PHI-reader' role. we recommend translating to boolean flags in SCIM (e.g. phi_read: true) to simplify policies.
04:40 Lydia: as a best practice we advise minimal attributes in the assertion and rely on SCIM for richer profile attributes to avoid bloat in SAML.
04:48 Tom: what about SCIM rate limits; if we do a bulk reconcile of 50k users how does Redwood handle that?
04:55 Evan: we support bulk imports with backpressure and async reconciliation. we'll advise a staged approach: import, reconcile, dry-run mappings, then switch to live. for 50k, expect initial reconcile to run over a maintenance window.
05:12 Maya: ok. can we walk through a sample role mapping? you mentioned 'developer limited' earlier.
05:19 Evan: sure, I'll share a template. (screen share) We have columns: role_name, allowed_actions, denied_actions, resource_scope. example: 'developer_limited' -> can call 'generate', 'embed' on non-prod models; cannot call 'model_admin' or access billing. map groups: 'engineering' -> developer_limited, 'sre' -> ops_read + escalation_tooling.
05:46 Priya: how do you prevent privilege creep over time?
05:50 Lydia: we recommend quarterly role reviews, automated entitlement attestation flows, and a SCIM-driven deprovisioning hook that disables API tokens when users are removed from IdP.
06:05 Tom: what's the behavior if a user is removed in IdP but still has active sessions?
06:10 Evan: session tokens are short lived by default (15 minutes for some flows), and we have forced session invalidation via revocation API triggered by deprovision events. there might be a small window but revocation is immediate once the event is processed.
06:26 Maya: we also need SSO SAML metadata — which bindings do you support? HTTP-POST, Redirect?
06:31 Evan: we support HTTP-POST and HTTP-Redirect for SAML, and we also accept signed assertions with SHA-256. we can consume IdP metadata URL or static XML.
06:42 Priya: SCIM provisioning: do you support PATCH and bulk operations?
06:45 Evan: yes, SCIM PATCH for updates, POST for creates, and we accept bulk import via CSV or SCIM bulk endpoint. our SCIM is mostly RFC-compliant but some vendor-specific quirks exist.
06:58 Lydia: quick commercial note — for Private we require a minimum contract and there are extra support SLAs for log retention and KMS integration. we'll share specifics after this call.
07:07 Maya: understood. one more: we want JIT to only create user skeletons with no data access until a compliance signal is present. can Redwood gate data-plane access until a certain attribute is present?
07:18 Evan: yes, policy engine can deny inference calls until 'compliance_ok=true' attribute is present on the user profile. that attribute can be set via SCIM or via an automated attestation workflow.
07:30 Tom: great. are there any known limitations around group nesting? we use nested groups in our IdP (groups within groups).
07:36 Evan: nested groups vary by IdP; we can flatten at ingestion but sometimes that requires an IdP-side rule. we'll test with your IdP metadata.
07:45 Lydia: ok let's talk pilot: proposed pilot — 2 weeks staging, 100 users, SCIM sync, JIT onboarding enabled, run a few role-elevation flows and verify audit logs in your SIEM. any objections?
07:58 Maya: sounds good. timeline wise we need the SOC2 docs before the pilot.
08:03 Lydia: we'll email SOC2 and ISO artifacts today.
08:07 Tom: and we'll send IdP metadata and SCIM attribute CSV by end of week.
08:12 Priya: and we want a short runbook for emergency key rotation.
08:17 Lydia: Evan will include a key rotation runbook in the handoff.

(Discussion continues, deeper technical Q/A and occasional cross talk, imperfect transcriptions below)

12:34 Evan: ...so for the KMS integration in Private deployments we actually mount a KMS connector that talks to your HSM, uh there is an extra step for trust provisioning, you'll need to create a key policy that allows the Redwood runtime principal to encrypt/decrypt.
12:50 Maya: wait, do we have to hand over the private key? no, just permissions to use the CMK for envelope encryption right?
12:55 Evan: correct, you never hand over private key material; operations use the KMS API.
13:04 Tom: is there HSM validation for FIPS 140? we need FIPS for certain workloads.
13:09 Evan: we support FIPS-compliant HSMs in the private bundle, we can include the certification matrix.
13:18 Maya: any gotchas about audit export to our SIEM? some SIEMs hate multi-line JSON events.
13:24 Evan: we provide options: flat JSON, line-delimited JSON, and a syslog adapter. we'll test your SIEM connector during pilot.
13:36 Lydia: ok wrapping up, recap of next steps and action items. thanks everyone for the time.

End of transcript.
